summary: Advance the open game-night reliability gate by building a bounded four-phone LAN qualification hand without treating browser tabs as four physical phones.
qa.four-phone-lan.session-recorder was the missing executable hand; qa.physical-four-phone-lan remains an external device/router/observation gap that code cannot self-certify.

Added evidence/four-phone-lan-qualification-contract.md for axm.four-phone-lan-qualification/v1 with controller-kind identity, 30-minute eligibility, explicit host attestations, privacy, read-only operation, recovery, and immutable external physical verdict.

Server telemetry now exposes additive per-session client kind, connected duration, drive and item counters, applied meaningful drive, heartbeat count, bounded RTT distribution, ignored actions, and resume count.
LAN Lab consumes telemetry GETs only, records authorityWrites=0, retains no session IDs, network addresses, user agent, or raw actions, and cannot change simulation state or the physical verdict.

Qualification receipts have a 30-minute ceiling and at most 128 recent transition events; machine eligibility requires one stable controller per P1-P4, at least 95 percent overlap, per-seat action/heartbeat/RTT evidence, reconnect, owner protection, healthy telemetry, and explicit attestations.

Added opt-in ?lanlab=1 host UI with four seat cards, 25-second/2-minute/10-minute/30-minute durations, start/stop/download controls, three never-auto-checked host attestations, privacy copy, and an external-review verdict.

The 30-minute held-out test passed 101 bounded snapshots, four stable seats, P3 disconnect/resume, per-seat meaningful drive/fire/heartbeat/RTT, owner protection, duplicate-seat rejection, partial rejection, compact privacy, and the external verdict boundary.
Initial live Browser panel rendered all four seat cards and boundary language at 1280x720; all physical attestations were false and the verdict was external review.
The first local smoke connected four controller sessions but did not admit lobby gas clicks as meaningful racing input; the run was rejected as insufficient rather than promoted.

A later active run proved ignored actions in durable per-session telemetry while the receipt owner guard stayed false because its rolling global action window aged out the signal under sustained traffic.

Qualification now admits the maximum of rolling global ignored-action delta and durable controller-session ignored-action deltas; the held-out test explicitly ages the global evidence out and still requires the durable proof to pass.

Background Chromium tabs were timer-throttled and synthetic clicks were too brief for deterministic hold sampling, reinforcing that local tabs are not evidence of four phones or intended-router behavior.

The final foreground local receipt ran 55.756 seconds of a requested two-minute smoke with four machine-ready controller sessions, 100 percent all-four overlap, one meaningful drive and one fire attempt per seat, nine resumes, owner guard PASS, and empty browser logs.
Per-seat RTT p95 was P1 9.8 ms, P2 10.3 ms, P3 8.6 ms, and P4 9.6 ms in the bounded local receipt; this is local transport evidence, not target-router latency proof.
The final receipt remained partial and ineligible, all three physical attestations remained unchecked, and physicalGateVerdict remained requires-external-steward-review.
Promoted package and health metadata to 0.13.0 / PLAYABLE ALPHA V13 · FOUR-PHONE LAN LAB READY; required paths and HTTP delivery include the qualification core, UI, contract, and test.

Final npm test passed 34 focused checks, presentation and both recorder tests, all race/track/variant/battle soaks, 30 virtual reliability minutes, restart recovery, and HTTP coverage; reliability heap delta was 5.3 MB.
Focused manifest and game-night seams had zero errors and one expected physical-phone warning; package-verifier selftest passed 15 assertions; all 10 package JSON files parsed.
Comparator remains UNKNOWN with zero missing capabilities; qa.four-phone-lan.session-recorder is available while qa.physical-four-phone-lan remains unknown.
Broad Game Hub verification reported nine failures, all in actively owned 016; games 014, 015, 017, and 018 passed and no foreign files were edited.
Complete Game Hub snapshot scanned 1875 files with 77 active files and seven active shared seams; all active shared seams were in foreign 017/018 paths and none overlapped lane 015.

Next native reliability evidence is an externally observed 30-minute four-real-phone run on the intended router with explicit host attestations and downloaded receipt review; target-hardware performance, human listening/attachment, deeper content, and steward approval remain open.

User explicitly requested that active operational memory be placed in the workshop; this segment preserves decisive events without private reasoning, raw browser traffic, repetitive telemetry, or deletion of canonical/user material.
